description:
Mission for Integrated Horticulture Development (MIDH) is a significant initiative by the Government of India aimed at enhancing the horticulture sector in the country. 

The scheme was launched in 2014 as a part of the National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture. 

It was introduced to promote holistic growth of the horticulture sector through an integrated approach. 

The primary objective of MIDH is to increase the area under horticulture crops and enhance productivity. 

The mission aims to achieve a targeted increase in horticulture production by 20 percent over a five-year period. 

It also seeks to improve the income of farmers engaged in horticultural activities by providing them with necessary support and resources. 

The scheme encompasses various components including production, post-harvest management, and marketing of horticulture produce. 

MIDH focuses on the development of fruits, vegetables, spices, flowers, and medicinal plants. 

The benefits of the scheme include financial assistance for various activities related to horticulture. 

Farmers can receive up to 50 percent of the cost of inputs for establishing new orchards. 

For specific crops like fruits and vegetables, the assistance can go up to 75 percent in certain regions. 

The scheme also provides support for the construction of polyhouses and shade nets. 

Farmers can receive assistance of up to INR 1.5 lakh per hectare for establishing polyhouses. 

For post-harvest management, MIDH provides financial support for the establishment of packhouses, cold storage, and processing units. 

The financial assistance for packhouses can be up to 50 percent of the project cost. 

Cold storage facilities can receive up to INR 1 crore as financial assistance. 

The scheme also emphasizes the importance of marketing and value addition to horticulture produce. 

Farmers are encouraged to form cooperatives and self-help groups to enhance their bargaining power. 

MIDH promotes the establishment of Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs) to facilitate better marketing of produce. 

Eligibility for the MIDH scheme includes farmers engaged in horticulture activities. 

There is no specific age limit for eligibility. 

However, farmers must have a valid landholding to qualify for assistance. 

Income criteria are generally based on the prevailing agricultural income standards set by the government. 

Farmers must also possess knowledge or experience in horticulture practices. 

The application process for MIDH involves several steps. 

Farmers must first approach the local horticulture department or Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK). 

They need to fill out an application form detailing their horticulture activities. 

Required documents include proof of land ownership, identity proof, and a project proposal. 

Once the application is submitted, it is reviewed by the local horticulture officer. 

The officer conducts a field visit to assess the viability of the project. 

If approved, the financial assistance is disbursed in installments based on the progress of the project. 

The timeline for application submission is generally aligned with the agricultural calendar. 

Farmers are encouraged to apply during the pre-sowing season to ensure timely assistance. 

Disbursement of funds typically occurs within three months of project approval. 

MIDH is implemented by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare. 

The National Horticulture Board (NHB) plays a crucial role in the execution of the scheme. 

State horticulture departments are responsible for the ground-level implementation. 

Farmers can contact the NHB at their headquarters in Gurugram, Haryana for more information. 

The NHB also provides a helpline for farmers seeking assistance with the MIDH scheme. 

The scheme has seen significant success since its inception. 

As of 2022, over 20 lakh farmers have benefited from various components of MIDH. 

The area under horticulture crops has increased by approximately 15 percent since the launch of the scheme. 

The production of fruits and vegetables has also seen a remarkable rise. 

The government has allocated a budget of INR 1,000 crore for the MIDH scheme for the financial year 2023-2024. 

This funding is aimed at expanding the reach of the scheme to more farmers across the country. 

MIDH also emphasizes the use of modern technologies in horticulture practices. 

Farmers are encouraged to adopt drip irrigation and fertigation techniques to enhance productivity. 

The scheme promotes the use of organic farming practices to improve soil health. 

Training programs are conducted regularly to educate farmers about best practices in horticulture. 

The government collaborates with various agricultural universities and research institutions for training purposes. 

MIDH also focuses on the development of export-oriented horticulture. 

Farmers are provided with information about international market trends and standards. 

The scheme aims to increase the export of horticulture produce by 25 percent over the next five years. 

In addition to financial assistance, MIDH provides technical support to farmers. 

Experts from agricultural universities are often involved in guiding farmers through the process. 

The scheme also encourages research and development in horticulture to introduce new varieties and technologies. 

MIDH has a significant impact on rural employment generation. 

It is estimated that the horticulture sector can create over 10 million jobs in the next five years. 

The scheme contributes to the overall economic development of rural areas. 

Farmers engaged in horticulture often see an increase in their annual income by 30 percent. 

The success of MIDH is evident in the increasing number of farmers adopting horticulture as a primary source of livelihood. 

The government continues to monitor and evaluate the progress of the MIDH scheme regularly. 

Feedback from farmers is taken into account to improve the implementation of the scheme. 

Overall, the Mission for Integrated Horticulture Development is a comprehensive initiative aimed at transforming the horticulture landscape in India. 

It provides farmers with the necessary support to enhance productivity and income while promoting sustainable agricultural practices. 

The scheme is a vital step towards achieving food security and improving the livelihoods of millions of farmers across the country.
